scenario: 今日个性化这边，一条线把多种用户行为放进同一套图检索，好在网页级候选里又准又快；另一条线发现不同用户能从不同基础模型里受益，于是按用户融合打分，而不是把表示硬拼在一起。百度已把多关系并行图检索铺到二十多个应用里，每天处理超过一千亿次请求，页面停留时长和日活都有提升。融合多个基础模型时，自适应打分比朴素拼接更有效，额外推理开销也远不到翻倍。两边都在问同一件事：个性化计算怎样用在真正改结果的地方。

papers.title: GPU-accelerated Multi-relational Parallel Graph Retrieval for Web-scale Recommendations
papers.authors: Zhuoning Guo, Guangxing Chen, Qian Gao, Xiaochao Liao, Jianjia Zheng

retrieval_meta.raw_source_name: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026

papers.summary: 网页推荐要从海量候选里实时召回，图检索却很难把点击、观看等多种行为放进同一种相关性。高并发时，各请求的搜索路径长短不一，遍历既容易顾此失彼，不规则的神经计算也会把 GPU 拖成瓶颈。GMP-GR 用多目标度量统一这些用户-物品关系，再做兼顾广度和深度的分层并行图检索，并在 GPU 上自适应聚合不规则计算。它已在百度二十多个应用上线，服务数亿用户，每天处理超过一千亿次请求。在百度移动应用两个推荐场景的测试里，页面停留时长分别提高 1.13% 和 1.19%。两个场景的日活分别提高 0.23% 和 0.50%。系统优化之后，两个服务的查询吞吐大约翻倍。
papers.abstract: Web recommendations provide personalized items from massive catalogs for users, which rely heavily on retrieval stages to trade off the effectiveness and efficiency of selecting a small relevant set from billion-scale candidates in online digital platforms. As one of the largest Chinese search engine and news feed providers, Baidu resorts to Deep Neural Network (DNN) and graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) algorithms for accurate relevance estimation and efficient search for relevant items. However, current retrieval at Baidu fails in comprehensive user-item relational understanding due to dissected interaction modeling, and performs inefficiently in large-scale graph-based ANNS because of suboptimal traversal navigation and the GPU computational bottleneck under high concurrency. To this end, we propose a GPU-accelerated Multi-relational Parallel Graph Retrieval (GMP-GR) framework to achieve effective yet efficient retrieval in web-scale recommendations. First, we propose a multi-relational user-item relevance metric learning method that unifies diverse user behaviors through multi-objective optimization and employs a self-covariant loss to enhance pathfinding performance. Second, we develop a hierarchical parallel graph-based ANNS to boost graph retrieval throughput, which conducts breadth-depth-balanced searches on a large-scale item graph and cost-effectively handles irregular neural computation via adaptive aggregation on GPUs. In addition, we integrate system optimization strategies in the deployment of GMP-GR in Baidu. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of GMP-GR in retrieval accuracy and efficiency. Deployed across more than twenty applications at Baidu, GMP-GR serves hundreds of millions of users with a throughput exceeding one hundred million requests per second.

papers.title: User-Adaptive Fusion of Multiple Foundation Models for Recommender Systems
papers.authors: Sunwoo Kim, Hyunjin Hwang, Geon Lee, Kyungho Kim, Kijung Shin
papers.summary: 把多个基础模型的表示直接拼在一起，推荐效果往往只比单模型好一点。真正的问题是，能从各个基础模型里受益的用户并不是同一批人，平均意义上的拼接很难帮到真正需要某个模型的人。UF2O 为每个基础模型保留独立的推荐视图，再按用户自适应地融合打分，不必先对齐不同模型的表示空间，因而也能融合异构模型。基础模型保持冻结，物品表示可以预先算好，多个视图的打分还能并行。在四个数据集上同时融合四个基础模型时，它在静态和序列推荐里都超过已有融合方法，相对最强融合基线最多提升 7%。尽管用了四个视图，平均推理耗时并没有变成四倍，只多了不到 60%。
papers.abstract: Can recommender systems benefit from combining a collection of foundation models within and across modalities? While different foundation models may capture complementary aspects of item metadata, we find that naively combining their representations yields only marginal gains over using a single foundation model. We make a key observation: the users who benefit vary across foundation models. Motivated by this observation, we introduce UF2O, a user-adaptive approach for fusing multiple foundation models for recommendation. In a nutshell, UF2O models the contribution of each foundation model as user-specific by maintaining separate recommendation views and adaptively combining their scores for each user. By performing fusion at the score level, UF2O can also fuse heterogeneous foundation models without directly aligning their representation spaces. Extensive experiments that jointly combine four foundation models on four datasets show that UF2O outperforms existing fusion approaches in both static and sequential recommendation settings, with improvements of up to 7% over the strongest fusion baseline. The code, datasets, and supplementary materials for our work are available at https://github.com/kswoo97/UFFO.
